To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the correlation functions of the responses of a buried pipeline are derived in closed-form and an illustrative example is given to show the history and correlation of the responses of the pipeline under earthquake excitation.
the non-stationary responses of buried pipelines under earthquakes are studied and a closed form expression of correlation function of the responses is presented.
the non-stationary responses of buried pipelines can be derived in closed form by using a non-stationarity model of earthquake excitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of non-stationary response of buried pipelines.
the dynamic response of pipelines under earthquake excitations and the effects of soil-structure interaction.
the non-stationary response of buried pipelines subjected to non-stationary ground motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the non-stationary response is a very important consideration in the analysis of the response of buried pipelines.
, the correlation of the ground motion is very important to the response of the buried pipelines, and the correlation of the response is also very important to the design of the pipelines.
the non-stationary response is a function of both the correlation time and the time of observation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the non-stationary nature of ground motion has significant effect on the response of buried pipelines.
the non-stationary responses of buried pipelines under earthquakes can be predicted in closed form by taking into consideration of ground motion correlation.
the correlation of ground motions and non-stationarity of random responses of structures should be considered in the study of earthquake engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the correlation of ground motions has significant effects on the responses of the buried pipeline, and the correlation of ground acceleration has a more significant impact on the responses than the correlation of ground velocity and displacement.
buried pipelines can sustain higher stress level than that predicted by stationary random vibration theory.

the correlation functions for the responses of buried pipelines can be obtained by a simple procedure, and they can be used to estimate the mean square of responses and the probability density function of the responses of pipelines under earthquake excitations.
